chunks: As for what was narrated by ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥasan, from ʿUthmān ibn ʿĪsā, from Samāʿah ibn Mihrān, from Abū ʿAbdillāh and Abū al-Ḥasan عليهما السلام, they said:
Regarding a man who has intercourse with a woman, then she menstruates before performing ghusl from janābah, he said: “Ghusl of janābah is obligatory upon her.”

So this report is to be understood as carrying a sense of recommendation, even if the wording of obligation has been used for it. Also, his saying, “Ghusl of janābah is obligatory upon her,” does not indicate that the ghusl of menstruation is separately binding upon her in addition to that; and if that is not the case, then it is possible that the ghusl be ascribed to janābah while still being sufficient for both it and menstruation, as indicated by the reports we have already cited, and by that which also clarifies what we have mentioned.

key_terms.الِاسْتِحْبَابِ: recommendation or desirability in legal usage
key_terms.الْجَنَابَةِ: state of ritual impurity caused by sexual intercourse
key_terms.الْمَرْأَةَ: the woman in the legal case under discussion

ai.seo_question: If a woman menstruates before performing ghusl from janābah, does one ghusl suffice for both janābah and hayd?
ai.summary: This passage addresses the ruling of a woman who menstruates before performing ghusl after janābah. It presents a report stating that ghusl of janābah is obligatory upon her, then explains that this wording may indicate recommendation or that one ghusl may suffice for both janābah and menstruation.
